Frozen scale: 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch (batch ~1023), 3000 Stage2 epochs, 3 levels x 256 codes. Open: exact baseline Euclidean cost convention (L2-normalised dot vs squared L2) not visible; mechanism is written to drop into either by replacing only the distance term.

STEP 2 — goal: choose a coupling position different from plain behaviour-weighted curved assignment. Design chosen: behaviour-graph LOCAL CURVATURE (edge triangle-closure cohesion) becomes a bounded per-item curvature rank rho_i; each code k of each level carries ONE learnable curvature centre m_k=sigmoid(mu_k); the Sinkhorn cost matrix is made C_ik = d_c(x_i,p_k) - beta_l*exp(-(rho_i-m_k)^2/(2 s^2)) with beta_l calibrated from the measured median nearest-code curved distance at init (alpha=1.0, derived not swept), s=0.25 = MAD of a uniform rank; a scale-free curvature-homogeneity penalty L_curv = E_P[(rho_i-m_k)^2]/Var(rho) trains mu inside the same pathway (rho -> g -> C -> Sinkhorn plan -> L_curv -> mu -> g). IDEA: cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1
TITLE: Behaviour-graph closure rank as a per-code curvature centre inside the balanced Sinkhorn cost, so coarse Semantic-ID prefixes group items that are homogeneous in local behaviour curvature.
MOTIVATION: In a generative next-item recommender the coarse SID prefix is the generation condition: an L1 token that mixes items from flat (broad, hub-like) and tight (clique-like) neighbourhoods forces the generator to model two incompatible transition regimes under one prefix, and the L2/L3 refinement then spends capacity separating them. The quantiser currently groups items only by embedding proximity, so behaviourally inhomogeneous neighbourhoods are silently merged into one prefix. If the coarse prefix is instead curvature-homogeneous - items of similar behaviour-graph closure share the coarse code - the prefix becomes a meaningful behavioural summary, prefix-conditioned next-token prediction should sharpen, and Stage3 test Recall@10 should move above 0.065. The mechanism is aimed at exactly that: it does not touch the Euclidean/curved reconstruction target or the codebook sizes, only who shares which prefix.
NOVELTY: Existing mechanisms here weight the curved assignment by transition counts, add a standalone hyperbolic loss beside a behaviour loss, or build a behaviour hierarchy in an unquantised latent. This proposal turns a behaviour-graph CURVATURE statistic (edge triangle closure, rank-bounded) into a per-item scalar, gives every code a learnable CURVATURE CENTRE in that scalar, and injects the centre into the baseline's balanced Sinkhorn cost as a bounded offset, while a scale-free curvature-homogeneity penalty on the SAME balanced soft plan trains those centres. Behaviour and geometry therefore meet in the cost matrix and in one gradient loop; there is no separate behaviour loss and no Euclidean quantiser with a hyperbolic suffix.
CHANGE: The level-l Sinkhorn cost becomes the curved Poincare code distance minus a curvature-match bump between the item's behaviour-closure rank and the code's own learned curvature centre, and a normalised within-code curvature-variance penalty on the balanced plan jointly trains those centres.
SPECIFICATION:
(A) Behaviour side (train-only, computed once, frozen). Build the undirected co-occurrence graph on the 24556 training items from the training sequences: edge (i,j) with weight w_ij = log1p(#sequences in which i and j co-occur within the baseline window); keep the symmetric union of directed transitions; binary adjacency A = 1[w_ij > 0]. For each edge compute the triangle count t_ij = (A*A)_ij = |N(i) ∩ N(j)| (sparse product, no dense matrix). Item closure coh_i = mean_{j in N(i)} log1p(t_ij). Because raw triangle statistics are heavy tailed (mean ~700, median ~6 in this graph), coh is immediately rank-uniformised with average ranks: rho_i = (r_i - 0.5)/n, r_i = average ascending rank of coh_i, so rho in (0,1), median 0.5, MAD exactly 0.25 for a uniformised rank; degree-0 items get rho = 0.5 (neutral). rho is stored as a frozen float32 vector indexed by item id.
(B) Geometry side. Per contract: c > 0, R_c = 1/sqrt(c), ball points x_i = exp_0^c(u_i) and p_k = exp_0^c(q_k) from the baseline's level-l item embedding and code embedding, d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-x)(+)y||). c itself is measured, not tuned: c = 1 / median_i ||u_i^(1)||_2^2 over the 24556 training items at initialisation (so the ball radius equals the embedding

scale), floored at 1e-8.
(C) Coupling. Per level l in {1,2,3}, a trainable centre logit mu^(l) in R^256, m_k^(l) = sigmoid(mu_k^(l)) in (0,1). Match bump g_ik = exp(-(rho_i - m_k^(l))^2 / (2 s^2)), s = 0.25 (the MAD of a uniformised rank, a property of the rank transform, not a swept constant). Offset weight beta_l = alpha * median_{i in train} min_k d_c(x_i, p_k) measured ONCE at initialisation in a single no-grad pass over the 24556 items (alpha = 1.0 documented default; the offset is thereby commensurate with the distance term without any sweep). Cost matrix C_ik^(l) = d_c(x_i^(l), p_k^(l)) - beta_l * g_ik. The baseline's Sinkhorn solver and marginals are kept verbatim: K = exp(-C/eps) with the baseline eps, the same iterations and the same uniform row/column marginals; the hard level index is the baseline's rounding k_i = argmax_k P_ik of the balanced plan P, never argmin of a bare score. Balance therefore still governs codebook usage.
(D) Loss. L = L_recon + beta_commit L_commit + lambda_curv * L_curv, with L_curv = ( sum_{i,k} P_ik (rho_i - m_k^(l))^2 ) / ( sum_{i,k} P_ik * Var_hat(rho) + 1e-8 ) summed over the three levels, Var_hat(rho) the measured variance of rho over the batch; L_curv is a variance ratio in [0, ~1] and is given the documented default lambda_curv = 1.0 (scale-free, not swept). Reconstruction, commitment, STE, the three levels, dimension, codebook size, optimiser, epochs, batch and seed are unchanged; reconstruction and residual recursion use the un-hyperbolised codes exactly as in the baseline.
COST: Per-step at the frozen scale, batch B ~ 1023 (24556/24): 3 levels x 1023 x 256 = 785,664 curved cost entries per step, each needing one tangent-space difference, one tanh/norm and one artanh (~40 flops) plus the same exp as the baseline's Sinkhorn kernel (the exp count is unchanged), and the L_curv accumulation (786k multiply-adds). Estimated +3% to +5% step wall clock, i.e. roughly +0.1 to +0.2 s per step at 4 cards and about +2 to +3 h over 3000 epochs, no extra epochs. One-time costs before training: sparse A*A triangle product on 24556 nodes (seconds to a minute at the retained degree), rho rank sort O(n log n) (milliseconds), and one no-grad beta/c calibration pass of 3 x 6.29M = 18.9M distance evaluations (seconds). Stage3 protocol unchanged, so its cost is identical to the baseline. Parameter overhead: 3 x 256 = 768 extra scalars.
HYPOTHESIS: For the coupling to be worth keeping, the balanced plan must become curvature-sorted, i.e. the mean |rho_i - rho_j| over item pairs that share an L1 code must be well below the random-pair value (target ratio <= 0.5) while the L1 codebook stays balanced (241-of-256 order of used codes rather than the collapsed 42), and the three-level collision rate must stay near the reference 0.065 rather than the collapsed 0.703. If that stratification appears and Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run, the prefix has become a behaviourally meaningful generation condition; if the L1 stratification does not appear, Sinkhorn balance has washed the offset out and the mechanism is dead regardless of recall.
RISKS: The Sinkhorn column marginals are near-uniform, so the offset can only reorder, not unbalance; if beta_l is large relative to the distance spread the plan degenerates to a curvature quantile partition and reconstruction quality (and thus recall) drops. Rank-uniformising rho discards magnitude, so a genuine two-scale closure pattern can be flattened. Degree

-1 items get a single noisy edge and therefore a noisy rank. A hub edge with thousands of triangles can still dominate the unnormalised coh before ranking. Single run, no seeds: seed noise is inside the reported interval, so a marginal recall gain is not distinguishable from noise; c measured from initial embedding scale may be a poor curvature estimate for later epochs.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Training-only item-level local curvature of the co-consumption/transition graph, i.e. triangle closure of each item's neighbourhood, expressed as the bounded curvature rank rho_i.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From training-split interaction sequences only, before Stage2 starts: undirected co-occurrence graph with edge weight log1p(co-occurrence count) inside the baseline window; t_ij = (A*A)_ij on the binary adjacency; coh_i = mean_{j in N(i)} log1p(t_ij); rho_i = (average ascending rank of coh_i - 0.5)/n over the 24556 training items; rho stored frozen float32 with a hash of the training-file list. No validation or test sequence is ever read for this vector, and it is not recomputed during training or for Stage3.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: rho, the graph, c, and beta_l are all computed from the training split alone at initialisation and then frozen for the whole run; Stage2 and Stage3 never write back into them. The frozen rho has no dependence on any validation or test interaction, episode or metric, so no evaluation signal can shape the SID construction. Stage3 retrieval/generation consumes the trained codebook only; the curvature centres are training-time quantiser parameters and are not tuned on any eval split. No per-epoch recomputation from evaluation traces, no test-time graph update, no leakage of the Stage3 sequence into rho or into the Sinkhorn cost.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature kappa = -c with measured c = 1/median_i ||u_i||_2^2 (floored 1e-8), ball radius R_c = 1/sqrt(c); Poincare distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-x)(+)y||) between exp_0^c-mapped item and code points; used as the metric inside the level-wise Sinkhorn cost matrix.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the quantiser's assignment step of all three levels - the cost matrix that the baseline's balanced Sinkhorn solver consumes - and, through the differentiable plan P it produces, inside the curvature-homogeneity penalty that trains the code curvature centres m_k. It does not act in reconstruction, commitment, or the residual recursion, which stay Euclidean and on un-hyperbolised codes.
COUPLING PATH: One closed loop: training graph -> closure coh -> rank rho -> match bump g_ik(rho_i, m_k) -> offset in C^(l)_ik together with d_c(x_i,p_k) -> balanced Sinkhorn plan P -> (a) hard level index via the baseline's plan-argmax and (b) L_curv = E_P[(rho_i - m_k)^2]/Var(rho) -> gradient into mu -> m_k -> g -> C. Remove behaviour (rho constant, g == 1, L_curv == 0): the loop is cut, the cost is the plain curved distance. Remove geometry (c = 0): the distance collapses to the Euclidean metric while g and L_curv remain, so the same plan no longer measures curved proximity. Neither side leaves the core computation unchanged.
COUPLING EQUATION: C^(l)_ik = d_c(x_i^(l), p_k^(l)) - beta_l * exp( -(rho_i - sigmoid(mu_k^(l)))^2 / (2 s^2) ), with s = 0.25, beta_l = alpha * median_i min_k d_c(x_i^(l), p_k^(l)) (alpha = 1.0, measured at init), and L_curv^(l) = sum_{i,k} P_ik (rho_i - m_k^(l))^2 / (sum_{i,k} P_ik * Var(rho) + 1e-8) where P is the baseline Sinkhorn plan of exp(-C^(l)/eps).
OBSERV

ABLES: (1) Stratified SID metrics: L1 hard ER, L2 distinct-prefix count, L3 collision rate, L3 refinement gain; target is codebook usage in the reference order (L1 used codes ~241/256, top-code share far below 31%) and collision near the reference 0.065, never the collapsed 42/256 and 0.703. (2) The new homogeneity diagnostic: mean |rho_i - rho_j| over item pairs sharing an L1 code versus random pairs, and the fraction of same-prefix pairs with |rho_i - rho_j| <= s, whose ratio should fall below 0.5 (coherence/adjacency/transfer-predictability diagnostics are recorded but not gated). (3) mu^(l) should spread away from 0.5 into distinct centres across codes rather than all collapsing to the batch mean, visible as the spread of sigmoid(mu) at the last epoch. (4) The judgement: frozen-protocol Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: rho set to the constant 0.5 for all items, g_ik identically 1, offset 0 and L_curv 0 (mu unused, gradient zero); the curved d_c cost and the baseline balanced Sinkhorn are retained, so the arm isolates the behaviour side. Switch exists in code (behaviour_on flag); no arm is trained with it this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c = 0 so d_c reduces to the Euclidean code distance while rho, g_ik, the measured beta_l and L_curv are all retained - the curvature coupling runs on a Euclidean metric. This is the same-capacity Euclidean control and is run as its own separate arm in a sibling round (directory reported in the mechanism arm's report together with the identical stratified table and the same Stage3 numbers); it is not run as an ablation here.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run: measured c > 0, curved d_c plus the rank-curvature offset beta_l * g_ik inside the baseline balanced Sinkhorn cost at all three levels, and L_curv training mu; one training run only, no early stopping.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
# frozen, train split only
w_ij = log1p(#train co-occurrences of i,j in the baseline window); A = 1[w_ij > 0]
T = A @ A (sparse);  coh_i = (1/|N(i)|) * sum_{j in N(i)} log1p(T_ij);  rho_i = (avgrank(coh_i) - 0.5)/n
c = max(1 / median_i ||u_i^(1)||_2^2, 1e-8);  s = 0.25;  alpha = 1.0
beta_l = alpha * median_i min_k d_c(exp_0^c(u_i^(l)), exp_0^c(q_k^(l)))   # single no-grad pass at init
d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh(clamp(sqrt(c) * ||(-x) (+) y||, 0, 1 - 1e-6))
# per step, per level l
x_i = exp_0^c(u_i^(l));  p_k = exp_0^c(q_k^(l));  m_k = sigmoid(clamp(mu_k^(l), -20, 20))
g_ik = exp( -(rho_i - m_k)^2 / (2 s^2) )                       # in (e^{-8}, 1] for s = 0.25
C_ik = d_c(x_i, p_k) - beta_l * g_ik
K = exp(-C / eps);  u,v = sinkhorn_iters(K, row_marg = 1/B, col_marg = 1/256)   # baseline solver, baseline eps, baseline iteration count
P = diag(u) K diag(v);  k_i = argmax_k P_ik                   # baseline rounding, NOT argmin of any score
L_curv = sum_l [ sum_{i,k} P_ik (rho_i - m_k^(l))^2 / ( sum_{i,k} P_ik * Var_batch(rho) + 1e-8 ) ]
L = L_recon(codebook hard codes via STE, un-hyperbolised) + beta_commit * L_commit + 1.0 * L_curv
grad: dP/dC through the Sinkhorn iterations (standard differentiable Sinkhorn), dC/dmu through g_ik, dP/dmu through the same chain; hard code embedding straight-through as baseline
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: training-split co-occurrence graph (frozen), the 24556-item frozen rank vector rho, level-l item embeddings u^(l) and code embeddings q^(l) from the baseline encoder/codebook, the trainable centre logits mu^(l) in R^256, the measured constants c, s, alpha and the ca

librated beta_l. Outputs: a per-level cost matrix C in R^{B x 256} carrying curved distance minus the curvature-match offset, the baseline Sinkhorn plan P and its plan-argmax hard level indices k_i, the scalar L_curv and its gradients into mu^(l) (and, through C, into u^(l) and q^(l)), and the per-code curvature centres m_k for reporting.
SAFEGUARDS: artanh argument clamped to [0, 1 - 1e-6] and ball points clamped to radius R_c (1 - 1e-5); c floored at 1e-8 and beta_l clamped to [1e-3, 1e2] x its measured median so a degenerate initial codebook cannot blow the offset up; sigmoid logits clamped to +/-20 so m_k stays strictly inside (0,1) and g_ik is bounded in (e^{-8}, 1]; Var_batch(rho) floored at 1e-8 and the L_curv denominator guarded against zero column mass; degree-0 neighbours get rho = 0.5 (neutral offset) and empty neighbourhoods are skipped in coh; the Sinkhorn solver, its marginals and the plan-argmax rounding are untouched, so the balanced assignment cannot be replaced by an argmin and the codebook cannot collapse; beta_l and c are computed with no_grad and detached at init so neither is a gradient path; NaN/Inf guard on the loss that skips the step and logs; rho, c and beta_l are hashed into the run manifest to prove they were computed from the training split only.
END IDEA
